clue.text: Fortune left in church near the altar

blocks.note: chance is luck or fortune
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A sum of money has been forgotten in a church, close to the altar.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church around the altar, reserved for clergy and choir.

clue.text: Without headrest, taxi driver gets irritable

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece sits around the other

blocks.note: a cabby drives a cab
read as head of rest: the opening letter of rest

explanation.surface: A cab driver deprived of a headrest on the seat becomes grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: Headrest is one word in the surface but splits into 'head' plus 'rest' for the wordplay; the letter goes inside, just after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby is an informal adjective for bad-tempered or grouchy, like a cross crab.

clue.text: Insecure at publicity given to break-up

blocks.note: an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity
a rift is a split or break-up

explanation.surface: Someone feels insecure about the press coverage given to a celebrity split.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adrift is loose and unmoored, so not secure or anchored.

clue.text: Voice support quite happily

blocks.note: to cheer is to shout encouragement
quite in the sense of completely

explanation.surface: A fan shouts encouragement for their team in a rather contented way.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerfully is an adverb for doing something in a glad, good-humoured manner.

clue.text: Hard on the ear without a joke

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: lug is slang for an ear
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A story that grates on the listener's ear because it lacks any jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the ear' looks like a homophone signal, but the ear is LUG holding A, with H placed on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A laugh is informally something done for fun, as in 'it was only a laugh', a jest.

clue.text: One making cuts journalist identified

blocks.note: a hack is a jobbing journalist
saw in the sense of spotted or recognised

explanation.surface: An editor who trims copy has been unmasked as a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed tool for sawing metal, so it is a cutting implement.

clue.text: It's touch-and-go following accident

blocks.note: to hit is to make contact
taken as written
to run is to go, especially to flee

explanation.surface: After a crash, everything hangs in the balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch-and-go' reads as the idiom for precarious, but split into its words it describes the whole clue: strike someone, then flee the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit-and-run is a road accident in which the driver strikes someone and leaves without stopping.

clue.text: Pretentiousness about books

blocks.note: ca is short for circa, Latin for about
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A complaint about showing off concerning reading matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant is hypocritical, sanctimonious talk, a form of affected or pretentious speech.

clue.text: Aim to take apart damaged lock

blocks.note: to split is to divide or take apart
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A burglar sets out to dismantle a broken door lock.
explanation.walkthrough: The lock here is a lock of hair, not a door fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A split end is a hair whose tip has frayed into two, so a damaged strand of hair.

clue.text: Group of women find Home Counties men to be cocky types

blocks.note: WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation
the Home Counties are the counties around London, in the South East of England
guys is informal for men

explanation.surface: A women's club decides the men from around London are arrogant.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British community organisation for women; the Home Counties surround London in the South East.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiseguys are smart alecks, people who are brashly self-assured and insolent.

clue.text: Match in sea green

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the following words, running across the gap

blocks.note: found running through the two words

explanation.surface: A paint or fabric colour match in a shade of sea green.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that agree correspond or tally, which is what it means for them to match.

clue.text: Works out perspectives on relative non-starter

indicators.note: a non-starter never gets going, so the word loses its opening letter
in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: aunt, a relative, without its first letter
angles are viewpoints or perspectives

explanation.surface: Someone figures out how different people see a family member who never achieves anything.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'perspectives on relative' places the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To untangle a problem is to sort out or resolve it, just as you work out a puzzle.

clue.text: Sort of beer labourer gets in advance

indicators.note: to sort things is to rearrange them into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A workman is given some kind of beer up front, before the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of beer' reads as a beer style, but 'of' belongs with 'beer' in the letters being sorted.
explanation.definitionFit: Beforehand is an adverb meaning earlier or ahead of time, the same sense as in advance.

clue.text: Attach label to small animal

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: An instruction to put an identification tag on a little creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer, so it is one example of an animal.

clue.text: Carrying fine pasty meal prepared for miner's companion

indicators.note: something prepared has been made up or worked into shape, so its letters are rearranged
carrying means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A good Cornish pasty packed as lunch to take down the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: The pasty is the traditional miner's lunch, which makes the surface feel like the definition; the companion is a lamp, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: The safety lamp was the miner's constant aid underground, a lamp designed not to ignite firedamp.

clue.text: Doubt if new net curtain has yard added

indicators.note: new implies the letters are made fresh, put into a different order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a new net curtain should be made a yard longer.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncertainty is the state of not being sure, which is what doubt is.

clue.text: After a drink, student trainee misses end of procession

indicators.note: missing its end means the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: cava is a Spanish sparkling wine
L is the learner-driver plate, standing for a student
a cadet is a trainee officer; drop its last letter

explanation.surface: A cadet who has had a drink fails to stay for the end of the parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A drink' is a single unit here, the Spanish fizz CAVA, not A plus a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalcade is a formal parade of riders or vehicles, a kind of procession.

clue.text: Something in the air made intern go crazy

indicators.note: crazy suggests disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An unsettling atmosphere drove a junior doctor out of their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something in the air' sounds like a vague mood, but it is literal: a gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen makes up about four-fifths of the atmosphere, so it is literally a component of air.

clue.text: Couple hire the band

blocks.note: a brace is a pair
to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: Two people book a band for their wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The band reads as musicians but is a ring of metal worn on the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is an ornamental ring or band worn around the wrist.

clue.text: Strangely, Claire never detects red herring

indicators.note: strangely says the letters appear in an odd, unexpected order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Oddly, the detective Claire never spots the false clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a misleading clue with no bearing on the case, a distracting irrelevance.

clue.text: Fight off weird sister

indicators.note: weird suggests something odd and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone repels an unsettling sibling, perhaps one of Macbeth's witches.
explanation.walkthrough: The Weird Sisters are the witches in Macbeth, which makes 'weird sister' feel like one fixed phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist an attack is to withstand it or beat it back, i.e. fend it off.

clue.text: Instruction to give bill to holder

blocks.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, an ad
a vice is a clamp that holds work steady

explanation.surface: A direction to hand an invoice over to the person holding the account.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is guidance or counsel on what to do, close to instruction in sense.

clue.text: Joint attempt caught out

indicators.note: out says the named letter is removed, leaving the rest

blocks.note: a crack is a try, as in have a crack at it
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A shared effort that ended with someone caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scoring C stands for caught; take it away from the word for an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack of lamb is a cut of meat, a joint in the butcher's sense.

clue.text: He may be  in danger of crashing

definitions.text: He may be  in danger of crashing

blocks.note: surface reading: a driver or pilot at risk of an accident
setter's reading: crashing out, slang for falling asleep

explanation.walkthrough: To crash, or crash out, is informal for dropping off to sleep, so the person at risk is merely drowsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepyhead is a drowsy person, one liable to nod off at any moment.

clue.text: Advice to consumer

blocks.note: surface reading: a shopper, as in consumer advice
setter's reading: what you tell someone eating a meal

explanation.walkthrough: Consumer advice sounds like shopping guidance, but the consumer is someone consuming food.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb is the imperative urging someone to finish their food, the advice given to an eater.

clue.text: Passionate about singer

indicators.note: about suggests turning round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: avid means keen or passionate

explanation.surface: Someone is enthusiastic about a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, a prima donna.

clue.text: Around most of settlement, worker has to go out for entertainment

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped
around suggests turning about, so the shortened word runs backwards

blocks.note: village, a settlement, without its last letter
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A worker in a small community must leave it to find some fun.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallivant is to roam about seeking pleasure, i.e. to go out and enjoy oneself.

clue.text: Excuse for one trailing after a Liberal

blocks.note: taken as written
Lib is short for Liberal
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A justification offered by someone who lags behind a Liberal politician.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used loosely to mean any excuse.

clue.text: Madman knocked over one container after another

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the word is turned back to front

blocks.note: a tun is a large cask
a case is another kind of container

explanation.surface: A lunatic topples one box after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutcase is a slang term for an insane or crazy person.

clue.text: Noise better when ends cut off instrument

indicators.note: cutting off the ends removes the first and last letters

blocks.note: a pip is a short high-pitched sound, as in the time-signal pips
better without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A musical instrument sounds better once its ends are trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The instrument is a laboratory one, not a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipette is a slender tube used in laboratories to measure and transfer small volumes of liquid.
